Penix might be available for Sunday's game against the Bears

        The latest injury in Michael Penix Jr.'s snakebitten career was particularly cruel not only for him but for his team, too. Penix took a hard hit to his ribs late in regulation, knocking him out for overtime of the Falcons' eventual 30-23 loss to the Ravens on "Sunday Night Football."Penix's injury is not considered serious, according to ESPN, who added that he could potentially play in Sunday's game against the Bears. Atlanta plans to exercise caution, however, and will monitor his practice this week before making a decision on his status for Week 6. Here's the hit from Tavius Robinson that caused Penix's injury:
Initially, Penix missed just one play — the one immediately following the hit — when Tua Tagovailoa entered the game and found Bijan Robinson for a 14-yard gain on second-and-20. Penix returned and threw a ball away under pressure, and the Falcons punted to end regulation.The Ravens took the ball to start overtime and produced a touchdown drive that lasted over seven minutes. Cameras panned multiple times to the sideline, where Atlanta's medical staff was working on/examining Penix's right ribs. When Atlanta came out on offense, Tagovailoa entered while Penix had a towel over his head, distraught as he could only watch from the sideline. After the game, Penix said he was emotional because he wants to finish games and is frustrated by how many times he hasn't been able to do so.
"I did take some throws on the sideline just to see how I felt, and I did not feel like I was gonna be able to give our team what we needed to help us win that football game because of the pain that I was feeling, so that's all that happened," Penix said. "I was trying to get out there. [I] feel like if we had the ball first in overtime, I probably would have been out there, but as we were sitting, what I was going through, it just started getting worse and worse as we were just sitting there. I was getting cold."Tagovailoa found Drake London for 20 yards on Atlanta's first offensive play of overtime, but got picked off by Kyle Hamilton on the next snap.
Though Kevin Stefanski said the team will need to conduct more imaging and testing before establishing a timeline for Penix's return, Penix speaking to the media is a good sign.
"Knowing me, I'mma be ready to go next week because I've sat out enough my career," Penix said. "... I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field."Michael Penix Jr. injury historySeason/TeamInjury2018/Indiana   HoosiersRight   torn ACL2019/Indiana   HoosiersFractured   collarbone2020/Indiana   HoosiersRight   torn ACL2021/Washington   HuskiesLeft   A/C joint separation2025/Atlanta   FalconsLeft   knee bone bruise, partially torn ACL      Penix, who missed the first two games of the season, had been a huge reason Atlanta turned its season around from 0-2 to 2-2 and is still afloat now at 2-3. The Falcons have now had four different quarterbacks play this season already: Penix, Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (who started the first two games) and Jack Strand (who relieved a struggling Rush in a 34-3 loss in Week 2).Penix's ability to push the ball downfield helped free up the running game and make the passing game, mainly through London, come to life. The Falcons would very much like Penix's self-diagnosed availability for Week 6 to be accurate, given how much the team has struggled without him.

title: USWNT aim to prove they are 'side-by-side' with World Cup champs Spain - CBS Sports
description: The USWNT lost 2-0 to Spain on Saturday, two early defensive errors proving costly despite their ability to grow
body:
The USWNT lost 2-0 to Spain on Saturday, two early defensive errors proving costly despite their ability to grow into the game as it progressed
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:14 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        CHESTER, Pa. — The cadence of international soccer means national teams usually have plenty of time to fine-tune their approach -- the U.S. women are no exception. Rare are the opportunities to prove a point quickly but as the USWNT gear up for a second friendly against Spain in four days, that is exactly what awaits them.With the Women's World Cup now just eight months away, the USWNT are very obviously in the pursuit of proving they can win their fifth title next summer. The point, though, is much more layered than that. Head coach Emma Hayes has spent the last two years arguing there are no shortcuts to the podium, every step along the way meaningful in some shape, manner or form and against Spain in particular, the point is even more complex. Despite a 2-0 loss on Saturday where early defensive errors were costly, the U.S. team actually rebounded strongly and put together a convincing display that showcased their ability to go toe-to-toe with the world's top-ranked team. Tuesday's rematch offers a chance to make that last point much more concisely."We have to tighten up on those things because actually, they didn't create a lot of chances and I think if we defend those moments better, it at least puts us into a stronger position," Hayes said Monday, "but I think once you go 2-0 down against them, then you are faced with chasing the game and I think probably the first 30 to 45 minutes, I think we lost our structure. I think the second half, it was all about us but you also have to score to win games."How to watch USWNT vs. Spain, oddsDate: Tuesday, Oct. 13 | Time: 7 p.m. ETLocation: Subaru Park -- Chester, Pa.TV: TNT | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: USWNT +165; Draw +230; Spain +140
Execution was a refrain Hayes used frequently in her post-match assessments on Saturday and again on Monday, in large part because the USWNT's game plan started to click as the game wore on. Some tactical tweaks were required at halftime but the U.S. team's impressive shot creation abilities were hard to miss, even if the ball did not end up in the back of the net. Sophia Wilson's case as the USWNT's No. 9 is as strong as it has ever been, her striker's instinct an asset on the day despite the result and likely to be a strength again on Tuesday."As forwards, you have to have a little selfishness," Wilson said. "If no one shoots up top, I don't know who else is going to shoot so we do need a little bit more of that. At the same time, balancing that with combining with each other. I think we have great players. Obviously the downside of this team is we don't have a lot of time together so those relationships take a bit of time to build but I think with the players that we have here, we have enough of it to be able to combine and create chances and it's just about finishing those chances. We didn't lack chances last game."Hayes' serious demeanor only masks her optimism so much, not only because of her players' natural talent but because of their determination to fix their problems. Trinity Rodman said Saturday that she and her teammates would be eager to review the game tape on their iPads on the trip up from Washington D.C. to Philadelphia, a determination that resembles the head coach's steely focus on the task at hand no matter how far away the World Cup might be. Hayes always finds a way to mix her praise with a challenge, this time an obvious one.
"You play the same opponent twice and there's things within that you can do a bit better and I think our team has a really good habit of bringing them things into the second game, but we have to do 'em," she said. "I say this many times, you can get away with things against weaker opposition. You just can't with [Spain] and so I'll be looking for us to apply that."Hayes previously said she was unlikely to make a lot of changes to her lineups over the course of the doubleheader, which are essentially a litmus test for her first-choice team rather than a time for extreme experimentation. It only makes her team selection for Tuesday's fixture all the more intriguing — any changes she makes could be revealing ones, no matter which area of the pitch she makes them in. She diagnosed the USWNT's shortcomings on Saturday as collective ones, not those that revolved solely around individual mistakes, keeping her cards close to her chest on the lessons she personally took away from Saturday's loss. No matter the team selection, though, the U.S. team will be tasked with demonstrating not only the range but the problem-solving versatility that Hayes has tried to program this team to have."I feel like now that we've reflected on the game, we had chances and knowing Spain, they're going to have the ball and to be okay with that and to not mix it up with not feeling like we're in control and we have the momentum," defender Emily Fox said. "I think with our team, we have a bit of everything and that's the identity of this team. If we need to go long, we go long. If we need to possess, we possess so really being able to see what's on the field and then playing that."
Hayes insists that her team is still not the finished product, understandable for a coach that still has around 10 games to go before the World Cup, a tally that includes next month's Concacaf W Championship that will serve as North America's qualification tournament. That does not mean she is underselling her team's progress since winning Olympic gold two years ago in Paris, saying her side are essentially neck-and-neck with Spain as the World Cup inches closer and closer."We have to get the details right in them situations so what is the gap?" Hayes said about the difference between the U.S. and Spain. "You could turn around and say finishing or preventing goals. Yes, that's part of it but I think when we analyze the game through our lens and what we know to be true to impact the result, I know what it looked like in 2023 to what it looks like now and Spain and USA are right side-by-side but maybe the confidence they have being world champions, there's an efficiency to what they're doing in that regard. I think our players are still building back in together, particularly players who've been out for a period of time."The great privilege of international soccer is that teams often have the luxury of time, the choice ultimately theirs to use it well. Hayes exclusively coached at the club level before assuming her current role two years ago, a type of job where friendlies are not a dime a dozen and so trial periods are hardly something a team can afford. The USWNT's ups and, in particular, their downs are always notable considering the program's prestige and aspirations but even in the imbalance of Saturday's performance, Hayes' argument that the team is trending in the right direction is a reasonable one. The imperfections are almost the point – the U.S. team has not played a major international tournament since the Olympics and has undergone a reinvention since; friendlies like these the only adequate way to prepare for a World Cup.
"I'm not worried about it," Hayes said. "If I'm here merely to protect a wins record, then I'll pick a lesser opponent but I'm not here to do that. I'm here to see how much has that gap closed with [Spain] and then how far away are we from that and keep working towards it because they're the best team in the world for a reason."The USWNT are understandably ready to change the narrative in this doubleheader on Tuesday, even if the narrative is not inherently unfavorable."I think the cool opportunity is we get to play the same team a few days later," Wilson said. "We get to rest a little bit but also prepare and make the changes that we need to but also focus on what we did well in the game and taking those into the next game as well. I think it'll be a completely different game regardless of the fact that it's the same two teams."
Hayes has just one ask after Saturday's outing, though."My big request to the team is start earlier," she said. "Start earlier with the things that really matter and that's what I've been encouraging us to do tomorrow."

title: USWNT Emma Hayes calls for more female head coaches across global game - CBS Sports
description: The USA boss praised some of the world's best women coaches and hopes more will get opportunities to lead nationa
body:
The USA boss praised some of the world's best women coaches and hopes more will get opportunities to lead national teams
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        CHESTER, Pa. - As the United States and Spain square off for the second time on Tuesday at Subaru Park, Emma Hayes was able to reflect on a notable moment that the game brings, even if it shouldn't be notable. Two women will manage the FIFA number one and number two-ranked teams, Sonia Bermúdez and Hayes, overseeing Spain and the United States, respectively.Hayes has been a trailblazer since beginning her coaching journey in America with the Long Island Lady Riders before eventually going on to build an empire with Chelsea's Women's Super League team, and her journey has now come full circle with managing the USWNT on their road to the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2027 in Brazil. So when she opens up about the state of the game, it's worth listening to, and Monday just outside of Philadelphia was no different."I've made no secret of the fact that it's really difficult, I think, for females in this space to, one, get an interview, two, get a job, and three, stay in a job. I think the standards for us are so much higher than our male counterparts because rarely do you see women who have gone and done a job, finish, whether they've been fired or they've left, get another chance. Doesn't happen for us females as it does for everybody else," Hayes said.   "But I also think, you know, it's Sarina Wiegman and Sonia Bompastor who are outstanding coaches. I think it's great to see that. I think we need to see more representation, and I'm a big pro that they made it mandatory for at least one technical member [to be female]," Hayes continued. "I'd like to go further. I'd like to see more female head coaches in national teams, because, yeah, I think it's hard enough getting into this industry as it is."
With Hayes advocating for these structural changes to the game, it highlights the broader soccer landscape. In the past, there have been some coaches who have been afforded the opportunity to coach the women's game who may not have been natural choices like Landon Donovan, Richie Burke, and Chris Armas, having no experience coaching women's teams prior to coming to the NWSL. Even currently, 11 of the 16 NWSL teams are led by male coaches.Those three were able to use playing experience and connections, mostly, in order to get their roles, which are common in soccer, but they also aren't ones that women in the sport currently have, as people like Hayes are leading the charge for women to get more opportunities.
The list goes on and on, and while Hayes is trying to create opportunities for more women to play soccer, it's also critical for there to be more opportunities to discover the next Hayes in this growing soccer landscape. Continuing to beat the drum on this to raise awareness is important, but as Hayes suggested, the sport's governing bodies need to go further to ensure that it happens by investing more in women to lead teams across the world.

Here's how to watch Rams vs. Bills, along with the latest odds, key matchups and our Week 5 'Monday Night Football' prediction

        In the Week 5 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Los Angeles Rams host the Buffalo Bills.The Rams are coming off a too-close-for-comfort win over the Philadelphia Eagles, having improved to 2-2 on in the process. They have not quite been the super team many expected, though injuries have played their part. They have a chance to get above .500 if they can capture a win against the Bills on Monday night.The Bills, meanwhile, are coming off their first loss of the season, having dropped a dispiriting game against the division rival New England Patriots. The Bills had started 3-0 behind a pair of explosive offensive performances in Weeks 1 and 2 and then a comeback victory despite turning the ball over five times in Week 3. Their defense hasn't been up to snuff, and the Rams present a tremendous challenge.Will the Rams leave the stadium with a winning record, or will the Bills bounce back from last week's defeat? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
You can follow along live here on our blog.Where to watch Rams vs. Bills liveDate: Monday, Oct. 12 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Rams -3.5, O/U 54.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Bills have the ballThe Bills gained more than 400 yards and scored at least 36 points in each of their first two games of the season, playing pristine football as they secured wins against the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions. They did not turn the ball over at all and they looked like an absolute machine as they worked their way through those two defenses with relative ease. Over the last two weeks, things have been a bit choppier, as the Bills didn't top 350 yards in either game and turned the ball over multiple times against both the Los Angeles Chargers (five) and New England Patriots (two), scoring 24 and 26 points, respectively. They were fortunate to escape with a win against L.A., but didn't get quite so lucky against New England and suffered their first loss of the season.The Rams, meanwhile, were torn asunder by the division rival San Francisco 49ers back in Week 1, but have since been incredibly stingy on defense. They've held each of their last three opponents under 260 yards, and two of them under 185. Their pass defense, in particular, has been remarkable, but the run defense has also been quite good since that first game. And they've done it without Myles Garrett (who got knee surgery following the Week 1 game) and, last week, without Aaron Donald (who is set to return on Monday after a one-game absence).
Buffalo is without wide receiver Josh Palmer on Monday night, and could be without No. 1 target DJ Moore as well. Moore is questionable after missing two of his last three practices. That could mean Josh Allen is down to Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Dalton Kincaid as his passing-game options, leaving the Bills shorthanded against what has been an excellent pass defense over the last three weeks and that gets Jaylen Watson back after he missed most of the last two games. Allen, of course, is capable of turning any group of skill-position players into a functional one, as we saw over most of the last two years before the Bills traded for Moore. It's worth noting, though, that the Rams have entirely shut down the tight end position so far this year, allowing 12 catches for a league-low 85 yards to players at the position. Kincaid could therefore have a tough time getting going here, meaning the passing game would have to run through Coleman (who could see a lot of Trent McDuffie, who is playing at an extraordinarily high level) and Shakir. Allen can obviously make that work; it would just be more difficult than if he had Moore in addition to the other weapons.James Cook — who led the NFL in rushing last season — is averaging an incredible and career-best 6.0 yards per carry so far this year, and has tagged two of four opponents for at least 135 yards on the ground. The Rams were run all over by San Francisco back in Week 1, but have since limited opposing backs in a big way. They haven't exactly faced a murderer's row of running games (Giants, Broncos, Eagles) during that span, though, so they could find it tougher to contain Cook here. Cook getting going would obviously take some of the pressure off of Allen and the potentially weapons-depleted passing game.
When the Rams have the ballAfter sputtering to just 290 total yards back in their Week 1 game in Australia, the Rams have put up at least 415 yards in each of their last three games stateside. The only thing that's kept them from truly exploding offensively has been turnovers, as they've given the ball away two times in each of their games so far this season — including those last three where they piled up all the yardage. After throwing 46 touchdowns against just eight interceptions on his way to an MVP season a year ago, Matthew Stafford has already been picked off six times. Stafford only completed 61% of his passes, and he's down from 7.9 to 7.3 yards per attempt. Stafford, of course, didn't have Puka Nacua for two of those games, but even with Nacua back last week, he was at just 62.7% completions and 6.2 yards per attempt while being held scoreless and intercepted twice. He just has not played up to last year's standard yet. Buffalo's defense, though, has been vulnerable through the air early on in the Jim Leonhard era. The Bills have gotten excellent pass rush from Greg Rousseau (who leads the league with six sacks and ranks third with 29 total pressures) and great play inside from Deone Walker (19 pressures and three batted passes) but the back end has been leaky, with opponents totaling the sixth-most passing yards in the league through four weeks, along with 10 touchdown passes against just two interceptions. 
Christian Benford returning to the lineup after he missed last week's loss against New England will help, but the Bills could still have their hands full with Nacua and Davante Adams — the latter of whom looks reinvigorated (career-best 10.3 yards per target) after repeated red-zone touchdown connections overshadowed a significant drop in efficiency last year. (He averaged just 6.9 yards per target, the fourth-worst mark of his 13-year career.) Adams was quiet last week against Philly (four catches for 32 yards on nine targets), but during the previous two games, he caught 15 passes for 332 yards and two touchdowns in Nacua's absence. It's worth noting that the Bills have given up the sixth-most catches, seventh-most yards and second-most touchdowns to running backs as pass-catchers so far this season. The Rams typically rarely target their running backs with the pass, but that has changed with Kyren Williams. Watch out for him on underneath routes.Williams and Blake Corum have also been highly efficient on the ground, combining for 87 carries for 456 yards and three touchdowns. That's an average of 5.2 yards per carry, and they each have success rates over 50% while Williams leads the league with a 64.8% rate on his runs. The Bills have given up only 0.98 yards before contact per carry so far this year, per Tru Media, but they've allowed 3.05 after contact thanks to one of the highest missed-tackle rates in the league. They can't allow Williams and Corum to slip out of their grasp here.
PredictionSo far this season, the Rams have alternated between looking like the Rams team we expected and a much different version than that. That's largely due to injuries that have led to inconsistencies on both sides of the ball. The pass defense has been largely excellent, though, and the return of Aaron Donald should help the run defense. I don't think Buffalo has anyone that can deal with the Puka Nacua-Davante Adams-Kyren Williams trio, so the Rams should put some points on the board here. Pick: Rams 28, Bills 24

title: SEC adopts standardized NIL contracts in latest step toward self-governance - CBS Sports
description: After the Big Ten implemented a uniform athlete contract model, the SEC has followed suit, with school presidents
body:
After the Big Ten implemented a uniform athlete contract model, the SEC has followed suit, with school presidents voting Monday to standardize NIL and revenue-share agreements
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        SEC presidents voted Monday to adopt uniform NIL and revenue-share contracts across the league, effective immediately, sources told CBS Sports. The SEC joins the Big Ten as the second power conference to adopt standardized athlete contracts. Schools can share up to $21.6 million in revenue directly with athletes this academic year, the second year of the 10-year window under the House v. NCAA settlement. Players received nearly $1.8 billion in direct revenue-share payments during the 2025-26 school year, according to the College Sports Commission.The SEC's new NIL contract includes customizable sections, sources said, but CBS Sports was not given specifics. The Big Ten drafted a standardized memorandum of understanding for its schools before the House v. NCAA settlement took effect in July 2025. The template allowed schools to tweak and customize the deals.
Public records requests in January 2026 revealed notable differences among member institutions in the Big Ten's standardized agreements. For example, Washington added a liquidated damages clause for a player entering the transfer portal, making him or the new school liable for the remainder of the contract's value, according to documents obtained by Kristi Dosh of Extra Points. 
        
            
                Multiple Power Four programs face College Sports Commission investigations over alleged NIL cap evasion
                
                    John Talty                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The documents also include provisions granting termination rights in the event of a head coaching change, medical disqualification or a violation of a morals clause. Schools can claw back a prorated share of money already paid in Big Ten contracts, according to a January 2025 Sportico report. The Big Ten also added a clause titled "No Employment," which requires the player to acknowledge he is not an employee and waive any claim that he is. 
When athletes sign an NIL agreement with a school, they grant the school rights to their name, image and likeness for use by the school, which are typically also sublicensed to the conference, the NCAA, TV partners and sponsors.The SEC circulated a suggested NIL contract template to its schools in 2025, according to ESPN, which obtained a copy at the time. That version barred athletes and their representatives from trying to "initiate, solicit, entertain, negotiate, accept or discuss" offers from other schools while under contract and required them to notify their school of any outside interest -- otherwise known as tampering. The Big Ten's NIL contract may have stopped Washington quarterback Demond Williams Jr. from entering the portal just four days after signing a deal with the Huskies in January. Washington and the Big Ten consulted, and with a potential legal battle looming, Williams opted to return to Washington and apologized for his actions, explaining that he had received bad advice. 
Similar battles have erupted in the SEC. Last year, Arkansas threatened legal action against quarterback Madden Iamaleava, who left the school in the spring after signing an NIL contract with Arkansas in January. The Razorbacks sought $200,000 from Iamaleava and hired prominent sports attorney Tom Mars to pursue legal action. Sources told CBS Sports that Iamaleava and Arkansas later settled out of court.As college athletics administrators await the House of Representatives' vote on the Protect College Sports Act following the midterm election in November, the SEC's decision to implement a standardized NIL agreement marks another step toward a self-governance model within the conference.Legal protections, however, remain paramount. In pro sports, union-bargained terms are generally shielded from antitrust challenges under the labor exemption the Supreme Court applied in Brown v. Pro Football in 1996. A contract drafted by 16 competing schools acting through their conference has no such protection now, though it could later, depending on the passage of the Protect College Sports Act, which promises limited antitrust protections. The protections include legal shields regarding revenue-sharing caps, NIL regulations, eligibility rules and transfer restrictions.
The SEC's presidents refrained from advancing another self-governance proposal on Monday, tabling a vote on whether to reinstate the conference's intraconference transfer policy. Before the restrictions were lifted in June 2021, the rule required players transferring between SEC programs to sit out one season.

title: UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava expected to miss remainder of season after knee injury - CBS Sports
description: Iamaleava exited Saturday's win over Oregon after suffering an apparent leg injury
body:
Iamaleava exited Saturday's win over Oregon after suffering an apparent leg injury
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Iamaleava exited Saturday's 17-15 win over Oregon after getting tangled up awkwardly between a pair of Ducks defenders.At his Monday press conference, Bob Chesney admitted there was "serious concern' but didn't officially rule out Iamaleava for the rest of the season."I'm gonna wait on our doctors to make the final call on things," Chesney said. "He has a meeting later today, and we'll have a lot more clarity on where things are at. ... There is serious concern at the moment, but at the same time, there's nothing that has been fully ruled at this time. There's still other opinions and people we want to talk to just to make sure everyone sees it the same way."A former five-star recruit, Iamaleava transferred from Tennessee to UCLA prior to the 2025 season, and he stuck with the Bruins after Chesney took charge. In his second season with the Bruins, Iamaleava provided some stability at the quarterback position, even if his numbers didn't jump off the page.
In four-plus games, Iamaleava completed 62.1 percent of his passes for 982 yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions while rushing for 144 yards and a score.Looking ahead to the offseason, Iamaleava will have a big decision to make regarding the 2027 NFL Draft. Iamaleava has the tools to be an early-round selection, but he may have to spend one more season at the college level to prove his health and boost his draft stock.When Iamaleava left the game against Oregon, backup Ty Dieffenbach entered and managed the offense well enough to get the win. The senior completed three of his six passing attempts for 43 yards and a touchdown.
No. 12 UCLA's first test without Iamaleava will be a home contest against 4-1 Wisconsin on Saturday night.Where do the Bruins go at QB?While Dieffenbach replaced Iamaleava against Oregon, that doesn't mean the starting role is his for the rest of the season. In his postgame press conference, Chesney admitted it will be a "week-to-week" situation and that Dieffenbach's mobility earned him the nod as the primary back against Oregon."We're really on a week-to-week basis here," Chesney told 247Sports. "This week, we felt like we had to run a little bit more with the quarterback, possibly. And that's where I thought Ty had a really nice week. And that put us in that spot. It's just one of those things. I'm sure if Madden had gone in there, he would have done a phenomenal job as well. But Ty was the guy we decided on based on the previous week of practice, and I thought he did a really good job. But Madden is going to be there the whole way through as well, competing and fighting for that position with or without Nico."
Although he performed admirably, Dieffenbach's appearance against Oregon was his FBS debut. A three-star recruit out of high school, Dieffenbach spent two years at Pitt before transferring to Cal Poly last season. He was the Mustangs' starter last year before transferring to UCLA in the offseason.In his lone season at Cal Poly, Dieffenbach completed just 56.8 percent of his passes for 1,305 yards, nine touchdowns and nine interceptions.Dieffenbach's resume -- or lack thereof -- probably leaves the door open for sophomore Madden Iamaleava, Nico's younger brother. A four-star recruit in the 2025 signing class, Madden spent a few months at Arkansas before joining his brother at UCLA.
Madden Iamaleava has even less experience, limited to one passing attempt in his career. It fell incomplete.This may be a scenario in which Chesney simply rides the hot hand from one week to another, but the good news is that the quarterback probably won't be asked to do much.How much does QB matter?The quarterback definitely matters, since the Bruins can't play someone who derails the entire offense. But can Chesney find a game manager between Dieffenbach and Madden Iamaleava? That may be all he needs.
If Chesney can get average quarterback play the rest of the way, then UCLA's College Football Playoff hopes are very much still alive because of how good the team is at running the ball and playing defense.The Bruins rank sixth in the country in rushing yards per game with 253.2, and Wayne Knight is budding into a national superstar at running back. That should allow UCLA to take some of the burden off its quarterback, whoever that may be.It also helps that the Bruins don't need to light up the scoreboard because of how the defense is playing. The Bruins are eighth in the Big Ten in scoring defense, allowing just 18.0 points per game, and they're especially good against the run, surrendering just 87.6 rushing yards per game.
That means the quarterback doesn't have to air the ball out to win. In fact, Nico Iamaleava wasn't exactly turning heads with his play before the injury. The elder Iamaleava brother turned the ball over three times against Oregon, and UCLA still managed to pull out a win in Autzen Stadium.

Rhamondre Stevenson and Woody Marks gain Fantasy momentum, while Chase Brown struggles and Chicago's passing game sputters
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:34 pm ET

        Know what was nice about Week 5? Not a lot of bad weather, and not a lot of field goals. Eleven teams put up at least 26 points, and plenty of big-time Fantasy studs came through. Our daily Fantasy Football Today podcast includes a must-watch Sunday night livestream every single week when the late afternoon games end. It's our chance to react to what happened across the league and give an initial prognosis on what will happen moving forward. It's a great place to celebrate ... or commiserate. So while there are far more than two winners and two losers from this week's games, here are the two winners and two losers I gave on our show. Please keep in mind: I never share "winners" who are obvious studs (like Jahmyr Gibbs), and I never share "losers" who are obvious bench guys (like what Bo Nix has become). Week 5 Fantasy WinnersPatriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson
He started in 48% of leagues, a number that will rise quickly with TreVeyon Henderson sidelined for who knows how long. Rhamondre Stevenson ran for 4.9 yards per carry, caught three passes and scored one touchdown. He remains New England's back for passing downs and goal‑line plays as long as he keeps the ball -- and that'll be the case even when Henderson plays. A big reason to keep Stevenson in high regard is his upcoming seven-game schedule. After a bye week, Stevenson will play the Jets, Bears, Dolphins, Packers, Lions, Chargers and Bills. This schedule is fantasy-friendly. Stevenson should perform as a reliable RB2 with some RB1 potential.
Texans RB Woody Marks
Like Stevenson, Marks took advantage of the opportunities created by the injury to his teammate. With David Montgomery sidelined with a groin injury, Marks handled almost every single RB snap and gave the Texans something they haven't had much of this year: rushing efficiency! Sure, the opponent had something to do with that, and the Texans' upcoming schedule has plenty of tough matchups in it. But after back-to-back weeks with short-yardage touchdowns and a big workload this past game, it's clear the Texans coaching staff sees something in Marks. That trust should yield the lion's share of touches in the Texans offense even when Montgomery comes back. You'll probably find yourself starting Marks in Week 5 as a low-end option, even against a difficult matchup against the Jaguars, who now have held opposing RBs to a slim, trim 2.5 yards per rush.Week 5 Fantasy LosersChicago Bears passing offenseWeeks 3 and 4 were majestic collaborations of great scheme, talent and timing. Week 5 was a mess. And while the return of Caleb Williams will mean good things for Chicago's scoring overall, it's Williams' off-script, feast-or-famine play style that sent his pass-catchers' numbers into a tailspin for their first two games. Plays designed for, say, Colston Loveland see the ball go to someone else. Poor Rome Odunze had just six targets from Williams in two games -- which is two more than Loveland! It's going to be difficult to trust any Bears pass-catchers, including Luther Burden III, given not only Williams' return but also their sorry play at Green Bay.
Bengals RB Chase Brown
It is time to lower expectations for Chase Brown. He has scored 12 or more PPR points in one of his last four games and has not scored a touchdown in that period. His snap rate against the Dolphins was 60%, and he wasn't even the leading rusher for Cincinnati -- Samaje Perine had one more carry! While Brown got away with a great PPR day last week due to heavy target volume, this matchup against Miami was supposed to be the game where he exploded for huge numbers. Instead, he managed just 39 yards on 13 carries (with a long run of seven yards) with very little room to work. For now, the hope is that the Bengals use their bye week to revamp the run game, but that may not mean they'll put everything on Brown's shoulders. Cincy's schedule ahead isn't particularly favorable, either. If you buy low, expect No. 2 RB results and hope to be pleasantly surprised.

        The 2026-27 college basketball season begins in less than a month, which means preseason predictions, polls and accolades are starting to trickle out before the season starts next month. On Monday, the SEC released its preseason poll ahead of the conference's media day this week, and, unsurprisingly, Florida was picked to win the conference.The Gators will be the favorite to win the SEC and the national title this season. And when the preseason AP Top 25 poll is released next week, Florida is expected to occupy the top spot. Florida had an incredible offseason of retention after bringing back four starters (Thomas Haugh, Rueben Chinyelu, Boogie Fland and Alex Condon) from a team that earned a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament for the second consecutive season.While Florida is the overwhelming favorite, other teams in the conference are expected to make noise. Among them is Texas, which was picked to finish No. 2 in the preseason SEC poll. The Longhorns reached the Sweet 16 in Sean Miller's first season with the program and are expected to open the season ranked somewhere inside the top 10 of the AP poll.
        
            
                SEC expert picks: 2026-27 preview, projected order of finish, preseason predictions, top players to watch
                
                    David Cobb

This season, Calipari is once again getting another stud freshman who should outperform his projection as a second-team All-SEC player. The 6-foot-2 combo guard can get downhill with ease and should be able to put up numbers. Smith should be the consensus favorite to win SEC Freshman of the Year.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Overrated: Malachi Moreno, Kentucky It's hard to single out any player on this list, but if I had to pick one, it would be Moreno, just because (outside of the lone freshman on this list), he is the most inexperienced returner. Moreno has a very high ceiling and should thrive in his second season playing in Mark Pope's system. However, if there was another player, I would've put on third-team All-SEC, it would be Crowe, who could legitimately finish as one of the leading scorers in the SEC, especially if Mitchell isn't cleared to play.

title: Oregon, Texas A&M among college football teams facing major regression in 2026 - CBS Sports
description: Growth isn't linear, and that's especially true in this current era of college football. A successful season one year is not a guarantee
body:
Growth isn't linear, and that's especially true in this current era of college football. A successful season one year is not a guarantee of another, and with how quickly rosters can change in the portal era, plenty of teams find themselves at the midpoint of the 2026 season wondering what happened to the optimism and hope surrounding their program last year. A wild coaching carousel last year added to the chaos of the portal, and a handful of teams who exited the 2025 season feeling like they were on the ascension have come crashing back to earth in 2026. That can be a tough pill to swallow, especially for those who felt they were climbing the ladder into a contender role -- either at a conference level or nationally. But six weeks into the season, there's nowhere to hide. While there's still time to salvage something positive from 2026, the reality is that these teams have taken a serious step back from last year and must identify how to begin climbing again. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    OregonThe Ducks began the season No. 2 in the preseason polls, but after a dismal performance at home against UCLA, Oregon's College Football Playoff dreams are on life support, and they're outside the top 25 entirely. Oregon has a strong case for the biggest disappointment in college football this season. While the Ducks' struggles against UCLA were compounded by Dante Moore's absence, this Oregon squad hasn't looked right all season. The offense hasn't been as efficient or explosive as it was a year ago, and the defense touted as one of the nation's best coming into the season has been merely good, not great. 
        
            
                Once a national title favorite, Oregon has become college football's biggest disappointment
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
How did the Ducks get here? For starters, their staff was hit by the coaching carousel, with offensive coordinator Will Stein now thriving at Kentucky, while defensive coordinator Tosh Lupoi has gotten off to a rocky start back at his alma mater, California -- although they picked up a needed win on Saturday. Dan Lanning opted to promote from within, hoping continuity could keep the Ducks rolling, but to this point, neither side of the ball has played up to expectations, and it didn't take long for those promotions to be second-guessed. 
At 3-2, Oregon still has a chance to reach the playoffs, but has no margin for error in its final seven games, which include a trip to Columbus to face Ohio State. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas A&MThe Aggies have likewise gone from a playoff berth in 2025 to a preseason top-10 ranking to out of the polls by Week 6. Mike Elko's third season in College Station has already reached the "antagonize the message board fans" stage, and after getting dismantled in Week 6 by Missouri, there are real questions about whether the Aggies will reach a bowl game in 2026. How did this happen? Well, like Oregon, the Aggies lost both of their top coordinators to the coaching carousel. Offensive coordinator Collin Klein took the Kansas State job and took co-defensive coordinator Jordan Peterson with him, while defensive coordinator Jay Bateman took the DC job at Kentucky. While the defense has held its own this year, the offense has fallen off a cliff. 
It's hard to know how much of that falls on the shoulders of Holmon Wiggins (who was the co-OC with Klein before taking the reins in full this season) and how much of it is a step back by quarterback Marcel Reed, but the Aggies quite literally cannot move the football consistently against decent competition. The Aggies scored six points against LSU and Mizzou, and while they finished with 21 against Kentucky, 14 of those came in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach. With Alabama, Tennessee and Texas still to come, there's a chance the Aggies are fighting for their lives just to get to .500, and the excitement in College Station has been replaced by anxiety in record time. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    WashingtonWashington was ranked in the preseason and was considered a potential dark horse in the Big Ten coming off a 9-4 campaign in 2025. Six weeks into the 2026 season, the Huskies have proven to be nowhere near contender status, and the excitement about what Jedd Fisch was building in Seattle has evaporated. 
The Huskies fought hard to bring quarterback Demond Williams Jr. back this offseason after he received overtures from LSU, but the offense has cratered even with the star QB back under center. The Huskies have not found suitable replacements for Denzel Boston and Jonah Coleman at receiver, as they now play on Sundays. Offensive coordinator Jimmy Dougherty moved down the road to work with the Seahawks, and Fisch opted not to replace him, instead taking over the offense himself. That's not yielded positive results, as the Huskies rank in the bottom half of the country in most offensive metrics. However, Washington's issues extend beyond the offense. The defense, which was winning them games to start the season, has begun to spring leaks, most notably yielding a season-high 41 points in a loss to Iowa on Friday night that set off alarms in Seattle. 
At 3-3 and riding a three-game losing streak, the Huskies suddenly find themselves trying to claw their way to a bowl game. Back-to-back road trips to Purdue and Nebraska look far more daunting than expected, and the Huskies end their season with an Indiana and Oregon back-to-back that won't be easy, even with Oregon's relative struggles this year. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LouisvilleLouisville began the year ranked, and after hanging around with Ole Miss and knocking off SMU in the first three weeks, it seemed Jeff Brohm might indeed have himself an ACC contender. However, since then, the Cardinals have seen their hopes of reaching the ACC title game implode with losses to Wake Forest (respectable) and NC State (brutal), before finally righting the ship against Florida State. Brohm has built his reputation as a big-game coach, but for Louisville to reach the top tier of the ACC, he has to figure out how to avoid the letdowns that always seem to follow those big wins. The defense has been leaky, allowing 30-plus points in four games already under new defensive leadership in Mark Ivey and Steve Ellis. 
That's put considerable pressure on Brohm's offense, led by Ohio State transfer Lincoln Kienholz. The offense has been good, but not quite elite, which is the level they've needed to be with a defense susceptible to big plays. After getting a fresh contract extension this offseason amid reported interest from Penn State, Brohm has ample job security, but his goal is to lead his alma mater back to contention in the ACC, and so far, he's not been able to get them to that level. At 3-3 with two losses in conference play, they would need some help getting to Charlotte. While the schedule doesn't feature any more ranked opponents in ACC play (only the final game of the year against rival Kentucky), the Cardinals' propensity to play up and down to competition is a concern with some opponents that won't get the blood pumping on their own. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    IllinoisAfter 19 combined wins over the last two seasons in Champaign, Bret Bielema had the Illini knocking on the door of the upper tiers of the Big Ten. However, a 3-3 start with losses to Duke and Purdue has instead proven they're closer to the bottom than the top in 2026. 
Illinois made a change at defensive coordinator coming into the season, bringing in former Montana head coach Bobby Hauck in what seemed like a coaching coup. Instead, it became a disaster, with Hauck resigning after four games as the Illinois defense ranks among the worst in all of FBS. The bright spot for the Illini has been the offense, with Katin Houser playing well after transferring from East Carolina, but he's now sidelined with a broken hand. The result feels like a lost season in Illinois, and while it shouldn't warm Bielema's seat too much, it is a reminder of how fine the margins are for teams in the middle of these power conferences. Illinois had put together back-to-back quality campaigns, but now seems more likely to finish below .500 than go on a second-half run for another. Bielema and his staff will have to spend the second half conducting an internal audit to figure out what went wrong and how to fix it for 2027, so they don't give back all their progress from 2024 and 2025. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Georgia TechThe Yellow Jackets won nine games in Brent Key's fourth season in charge, seemingly taking a major step forward as a program. Key was rewarded with a handsome contract extension to keep him in Atlanta, but the Tech faithful may be feeling a touch of buyer's remorse midway through the 2026 season. Georgia Tech lost quarterback Haynes King to the NFL and offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner and backup quarterback Aaron Philo to Florida, where the Gators got off to a fast start this season, only adding to the frustration in Atlanta. The Yellow Jackets pulled in Alberto Mendoza in the transfer portal, but the reigning Heisman Trophy winner's younger brother has not been able to get the Tech offense into much of a rhythm. After building their identity on running the ball under Key -- tied for fourth in rushing success rate a year ago -- the Yellow Jackets have fallen off considerably as a rushing attack in 2026. A suspect offensive line runs counter to everything Key is about, and when a team loses its ability to do what made it effective so quickly, it raises serious concerns. 
A win against Duke this past Saturday stopped the bleeding in Atlanta and gave Key a moment to breathe, but at 2-4, the Yellow Jackets have lost any margin for error after their slow start. The rest of this season is about trying to restate their identity as a tough, physical team to avoid questions about whether the foundation Key seemed to have built has cracks.

title: Texas A&M's Mike Elko apologizes for 'cesspool' comment, criticism of fans - CBS Sports
description: Elko drew backlash for his characterization of a section of the Aggies' fan base following Saturday's 21-point lo
body:
Elko drew backlash for his characterization of a section of the Aggies' fan base following Saturday's 21-point loss to Missouri
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It took about 48 hours for Mike Elko to walk back his criticism of Texas A&M's online fan base in the wake of a lopsided 27-6 loss to Missouri.In his postgame press conference on Saturday, Elko referred to "Billy's cesspool" when differentiating the fan base at large from those who criticize the Aggies on social media. It was a thoughtless answer that drew plenty of justified criticism across college football media, including CBS Sports' Brandon Marcello.On Monday, Elko apologized to the fans and to Billy Liucci, the co-owner of the popular TexAgs fan site."I think in the heat of the moment, I answered a question in a way that I certainly regret," Elko said during his press conference. "I think everybody knows I have a tremendous relationship with Billy. I appreciate Billy. I appreciate him being here today. There's nothing about Billy and I that have ever been off since 2018. I think everybody knows I appreciate our fan base and everything that they're about and everything that they mean to Texas A&M.
"And outside of that, I'll leave it alone. I regret the way it was taken. I regret the way it came out. I regret the way it ran. And so that certainly was never my intention."Elko's original comments stemmed from what has devolved into a highly disappointing season for Texas A&M. The Aggies started the year at No. 8 in the AP Top 25 poll, and they now sit at 1-3 in conference play with a tough schedule down the stretch. The latest loss was especially concerning, as Texas A&M mustered just six points against Missouri, with starting quarterback Marcel Reed completing fewer than 50% of his passes for 187 yards and two interceptions.
Texas A&M has already taken a clear step back from its 11-2 campaign in 2025. The only question left is how steep that drop-off will be.

title: Deebo Samuel injury: 49ers' wideout expected to miss multiple weeks with hamstring injury - CBS Sports
description: Samuel's injury occurred late in Sunday's win over Seattle
body:
Samuel's injury occurred late in Sunday's win over Seattle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Another day, another notable 49ers injury to monitor. This time, it's wideout Deebo Samuel, who injured his hamstring during the second half of San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. Samuels underwent further evaluation on Monday, and 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said that Samuel will be out "at least a couple of weeks." San Francisco will host Washington next week on "Monday Night Football." It will then face the Falcons in Atlanta in Week 7 before a Week 8 bye. The injury occurred late in the third quarter with the 49ers trailing, 23-21. Samuel stayed on the ground for several moments after committing the 49ers' second turnover of the quarter. He fumbled the ball while running after a catch, and the turnover led to a Seattle field goal. 
The 49ers responded with consecutive scoring drives. The first ended with a Brock Purdy touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks, who was recently signed to help the 49ers navigate through their injuries at receiver. The second drive was capped off by Eddy Pineiro's 44-yard field goal that proved to be the game-winning score. 
San Francisco received a big game from Mike Evans, who caught seven passes for 113 yards and a score despite having two fractured ribs. 
Evans and Cooks will have to continue to pick up the slack in Samuel's absence during the next several weeks. Samuel, 30, has had a successful reunion with the 49ers, who re-signed him this offseason after he spent the 2025 season with the Commanders. He's currently tied for second on the team with three touchdown catches and is second in receptions. He also has four runs that have resulted in first downs. 
Despite their injuries, the 49ers are one of only three teams that are still undefeated. San Francisco currently has a two-game cushion over the rest of the field in the NFC West division.

title: Is DJ Moore playing on 'Monday Night Football?' A look at the Bills WR's status vs. Rams - CBS Sports
description: Moore was initially listed as questionable with a shoulder injury

        The Buffalo Bills will help conclude Week 5 in the NFL when they roll into SoFi Stadium for a "Monday Night Football" heavyweight matchup with the Los Angeles Rams. This could very well be a Super Bowl preview between two of the league's elite clubs, but  Buffalo won't be firing on all cylinders offensively as top wideout DJ Moore is officially inactive for the contest as he continues to deal with a nagging shoulder injury. After not practicing on Thursday or Friday because of the ailment, Moore returned to the practice field on Saturday in a limited capacity, which held out hope and led to his questionable designation. On Monday afternoon, the Bills elevated wide receiver Trent Sherfield Sr. from the practice squad, indicating that Moore was truly a game-time decision. 
Moore, who was acquired by the Bills this offseason in a trade with the Chicago Bears, initially suffered the injury in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions. He has yet to miss a game due to the injury, but it has lingered, and he re-aggravated it in the second quarter of last week's loss to the New England Patriots. 
When Moore has been on the field, he's been the type of top target that the Bills were hoping to give Josh Allen when they struck the deal with Chicago. Through four games, Moore has caught 12 balls for 178 yards and a touchdown. While those are modest numbers, the injury has helped keep the production deflated. That said, in the two games he did not leave with an injury, Moore was a go-to resource for Allen in the passing game. In Week 1, Moore hauled in five of his eight targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in a win over Houston. Then, in Week 3, he caught six of a season-high 10 targets for 67 yards. In those two games, Moore commanded a 28.6% and a 38.5% target share, respectively. Moore is second on the team in red zone targets (3), and nine of his 12 receptions have gone for first downs. Keon Coleman will need to step up Former second-round pick Keon Coleman will need to carry more of the receiving workload. Coleman is coming off arguably the best game of his career, catching six passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in last week's loss to New England. Those six catches were tied for the second-most in a game in his career, while his receiving yards were also second-best of his career. 
In Week 4, five of Coleman's six catches went for first downs, and he averaged 12.8 air yards per target. That quantifies just how much of an explosive weapon he was in that contest, and he finished the game with four of his catches going for 16-plus yards.

        Awards season has arrived in the WNBA. Ironically, the first two awards announced -- Olivia Miles, Rookie of the Year and Cheryl Reeve, Coach of the Year -- were won by members of the Minnesota Lynx who were eliminated from the playoffs by the New York Liberty, becoming the first No. 1 seed to lose to a No. 8 seed in the first round in WNBA history. Since then, Dallas Wings forward Jessica Shepard (Most Improved Player), Atlanta Dream Angel Reese (Defensive Player of the Year) and Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün (Sixth Player of the Year) have joined the honorees. As has A'ja Wilson, who won her fifth MVP award and became the first player to win that award in three consecutive seasons. Reeve also added another Executive of the Year award to her trophy case this week.All major individual awards have now been announced, but still to come are the All-WNBA, All-Defensive and All-Rookie Teams, as well as the Sportsmanship award. 
        
            
                2026 WNBA awards ballot: Revealing picks for All-WNBA, All-Defensive, Most Improved and more
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rookie of the Year: Olivia Miles, LynxMiles, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, was named the unanimous Rookie of the Year as expected. She is the sixth player to win that honor unanimously, joining Aliyah Boston, A'ja Wilson, Elena Delle Donne, Tina Charles and Candace Parker. 
Miles, who averaged 19.8 points and six assists per game, led all rookies in scoring and assists, and finished eighth and seventh in the league, respectively, in those categories. She also broke Caitlin Clark's rookie points record (790) and led the Lynx to a 33-11 record and the No. 1 seed. 
        
            
                Was Olivia Miles a better rookie than Caitlin Clark? Comparing the WNBA's two best rookie guard seasons ever
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Most Improved Player: Jessica Shepard, WingsShepard joined the Wings in free agency on a two-year, $2 million deal that she immediately justified. As a full-time starter for the first time in her career, Shepard averaged 14.5 points, 11.1 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game, up from eight points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists last season. She finished second in the league in rebounding and 11th in assists, was one of two players (along with Angel Reese) to average a double-double, led the league with six triple-doubles and recorded just the second 20-20-10 game in WNBA history. Shepard beat out Shakira Austin and Carla Leite in a close race. Marina Mabrey, Dominique Malonga and Rae Burrell also received votes.

    Coach of the Year: Cheryl Reeve, LynxThe Lynx lost six rotation players from last season's team that went 34-10, and star forward Napheesa Collier was sidelined until late July after undergoing surgery on both ankles in the offseason, yet the Lynx once again finished with the best record in the league. That was thanks in large part to a tremendous coaching performance from Reeve, who helped turn Miles into one of the league's best players and got her new-look group to gel -- at least until the playoffs. Reeve has now won Coach of the Year five times, extending her record and becoming the first coach in major American professional sports to receive the honor five times. Reeve beat out Natalie Nakase and Sydney Johnson. CoachTeamVotesCheryl ReeveLynx40Natalie NakaseValkyries20Sydney JohnsonMystics14

    Sixth Player of the Year: Janelle Salaün, Golden State ValkyriesAs expected, Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün was named Sixth Player of the Year. She is first player in WNBA history to win the honor unanimously. The Frenchwoman led all bench scorers with 12.7 points per game, and shot 39.2% from 3-point range to help the Valkyries win a franchise record 32 games and earn the No. 2 seed. Thanks in part to the extended 44-game regular season, Salaün set WNBA single-season records for points (509), 3s (93) and double-digit scoring games (27) by a reserve. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MVP: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas AcesA'ja Wilson has done it again. After yet another historic season, the Las Vegas Aces star was named the 2026 WNBA MVP, becoming the first five-time MVP in league history and the first player to win the award in three consecutive seasons. Wilson took 65 of the 74 first-place votes, finishing ahead of Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles and Indiana Fever teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark. Miles received six first-place votes while Mitchell and Clark garnered two and one, respectively. This season, Wilson averaged 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.9 blocks on 52.7/40.4/86.4 shooting splits. Only a dozen made free throws prevented her from joining the vaunted 50/40/90 club; her 62.5% true shooting was 6.4% above the league average.
